name: Riverfront Streets of Suzhou: Beauty and Uniqueness
description: Method replication: same task, scales and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (47 new places on canal-side and moat-side roads in Gusu District, Suzhou, each as four Baidu street views facing north, east, south and west, captured 2019–2022). Original study: Xiong, Wu, Ma, Yang, Zhang, Zhang, Ye & Hu (2025), Land 14(10): 2039, doi:10.3390/land14102039. The authors sampled points every 50 m on riverfront streets in Gusu District, took Baidu street views in four directions (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°), and showed 48 randomly drawn points (four photos each) to 30 students and staff for 5 s each in random order while recording eye movements; afterwards participants rated each point for "beautiful" (aesthetic value) and "unique" (distinctiveness) on a 7-point scale from very poor (1) to excellent (7). Ratings were z-standardised within each rater and related to landscape elements found by semantic segmentation. Differences from the original study: (1) the points come from 8 road segments along the canals and the city moat that we chose by hand, not from 50-m sampling of OpenStreetMap riverfront roads, and the water is visible in only some of them; (2) 47 places instead of 48 (one point inside a tunnel was dropped); (3) the four photos are shown together as a 2×2 grid, with the ratings unlocked after 5 s on the same screen instead of a separate eye-tracking session followed by a questionnaire; (4) no eye tracking.
author: Xiong et al.
